references.text: A similar curse about losing children who are taken away, part of the same curse sequence in Deuteronomy.
Nehemiah describes how the people were scattered among the nations, a fulfillment of the curse concerning children given to other peoples.
Lamentations describes eyes failing from weeping over Jerusalem's destruction, parallel to eyes longing for their children.
Laban complains that his daughters and grandchildren are taken from him, thematically parallel to the pain of losing children.
Law regarding ransom money for daughters sold as slaves, related to the theme of children given to other peoples.
The description of Israel's exile to Assyria, a historical fulfillment of the curse.
